description: Starting source list for Farfield. Add, mute, or use only your own sources.

sources.name: Hugging Face daily papers
sources.access: Daily shortlist, not all arXiv. Keep first publication and featured dates separate. Deduplicate by arXiv ID.

sources.name: Martin Alderson
sources.why: Firsthand work on agent speed, costs, infrastructure, and software economics.
sources.access: Public RSS and articles.

sources.name: Every
sources.why: Workflows, creative practice, and organizational adoption from people building with AI.
sources.access: Public pages/previews only. Full-text RSS is a personal paid-subscriber feed in Account settings; never put that private URL in the catalog.

sources.name: Hamel Husain
sources.why: Task-specific evaluations and failure analysis from real AI projects.
sources.access: Public RSS and articles.

sources.name: Eugene Yan
sources.why: Production ML, retrieval, evaluation, and deployment tradeoffs.
sources.access: Public RSS; irregular cadence. Follow original article links.

sources.name: Ahead of AI (Sebastian Raschka)
sources.why: Technical explanations connecting papers to model training and evaluation.
sources.access: RSS can be large; some posts may be subscriber-only. Read accessible text only.

sources.name: AI as Normal Technology
sources.why: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor on evaluation quality, adoption, and limits of AI claims.
sources.access: Public feed; follow originals and distinguish arguments from empirical results.

sources.name: METR
sources.why: Independent evaluations of agent capabilities and effects on real work.
sources.access: Public RSS and reports; preserve task definitions and uncertainty.

sources.name: Epoch AI
sources.why: Measurement of compute, capabilities, inference, and economic adoption.
sources.access: Public Atom feed and reports.

sources.name: Anthropic Research
sources.why: Primary experiments in model behavior, safety, and economic use.
sources.access: Public index and articles. Vendor research; same family as Anthropic Engineering.

sources.name: Anthropic Engineering
sources.why: Concrete harness, evaluation, and tool-use implementation lessons.
sources.access: Public index. Some entries also appear in Research; deduplicate canonical article URLs.

sources.name: Berkeley AI Research
sources.why: Researchers explain their own work in learning, robotics, and systems.
sources.access: Public RSS with only a short recent list; inspect the blog archive for older windows.

sources.name: Hugging Face Blog
sources.why: Open model tooling, reproducible implementations, datasets, and practical experiments.
sources.access: Public feed; includes community and vendor posts. Follow primary code and paper links.

sources.name: Google DeepMind
sources.why: Primary work in models, robotics, and scientific applications.
sources.access: Public paginated index; distinguish research evidence from product announcements.

sources.name: Stanford HAI
sources.why: Research on adoption, labor, institutions, and the social effects of AI.
sources.access: Public news index; follow the underlying paper or report rather than treating the news summary as evidence.

sources.name: Benedict Evans
sources.why: Technology adoption and business-model analysis beyond individual model launches.
sources.access: Public essay feed; not the entire paid newsletter.

sources.name: Construction Physics
sources.why: Mechanisms of technological diffusion, production, and cost improvement outside software.
sources.access: RSS; some content may be paid. Use only when it illuminates an actual user question.

sources.name: Works in Progress
sources.why: Detailed accounts of scientific, institutional, and industrial progress.
sources.access: Public archive; distinguish magazine pieces from the separate newsletter.

sources.name: Chip Huyen
sources.why: Systematic explanations of AI systems and product tradeoffs.
sources.access: Public RSS; sparse/older feed. Do not represent an old essay as a recent publication.

sources.name: Lilian Weng
sources.why: Deep technical surveys linking methods, papers, and limitations.
sources.access: Public RSS, infrequent publication. Older surveys are background, not new findings.

sources.name: arXiv targeted searches
sources.why: Find recent work related to the user’s questions without relying on popularity-ranked lists.
sources.access: Public Atom API. Build dated, narrow queries; abstracts are discovery, not full-paper evidence.

sources.name: Practical AI
sources.access: Publisher transcript links in VTT, SRT and JSON via podcast:transcript.
sources.why: Applied ML systems and practitioner interviews.

sources.name: How I AI with Claire Vo
sources.access: Full transcripts on corresponding Lenny’s episode pages; follow episode links.
sources.why: Demonstrations of how people actually use AI at work.

sources.name: The Pragmatic Engineer Podcast
sources.access: Mixed newsletter and podcast feed. Select podcast entries; use published transcript text, not paid previews.
sources.why: Engineering practice, developer productivity and organizational adoption.

sources.name: Lenny’s Podcast
sources.why: Product decisions, growth and firsthand accounts of adopting AI.
sources.access: Mixed newsletter feed; filter Lenny’s Podcast episodes. Transcript availability and paid access vary. Use accessible published transcripts, never treat a Transcript tab or show notes as proof of full text.

sources.name: The Every Podcast (formerly AI & I)
sources.why: Conversations and demonstrations about AI and how people work.
sources.access: Publisher episode archive with pagination and separate transcript pages. Follow the transcript link and check access; deduplicate episode and transcript pages against Every’s main index.
